sense: a part of a group: one of them, many of us

terms.grammar: ūnus with ex, ē or dē and the ablative
evidence: Liv. 2.13.6: Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus
terms.comment: With ūnus, other numbers and quīdam, ex is commoner than the genitive: ūnus ex illīs, one of them; quīdam ex amīcīs, one of my friends.

terms.gloss: of (the group a part is taken from): many of them, none of you
terms.grammar: construction: the genitive of the whole; of persons, nostrum, vestrum
terms.comment: After words of number and quantity: multī eōrum, many of them; plērīque agricolārum, most farmers; quis vestrum?, which of you? “Of us, of you” here is nostrum, vestrum; nostrī, vestrī are the object of a feeling (memor nostrī, mindful of us).

terms.gloss: all of us, few of you: when the number is the whole group
terms.grammar: construction: the number agrees with the pronoun, or with the verb’s person; no genitive
terms.comment: When the number is the whole group, it agrees: nōs omnēs, all of us; trecentī conjūrāvimus, three hundred of us have sworn; Quot estis?, how many of you are there? The genitive of nōs omnēs is omnium nostrum.

phrases.english: Which of you opened the window?

phrases.latin: Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus … Tiberim trānāvit
phrases.english: the girl Cloelia, one of the hostages, swam across the Tiber

phrases.latin: Ūnus autem ex illīs, ut vīdit quia mundātus est, regressus est
phrases.english: and one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back

phrases.latin: cum quīdam ex ejus adsentātōribus, Damoclēs, commemorāret in sermōne cōpiās ejus
phrases.english: when one of his flatterers, Damocles, was talking of his wealth

phrases.latin: imperium summum Rōmae habēbit quī vestrum prīmus, ō juvenēs, ōsculum mātrī tulerit
phrases.english: the highest power at Rome will be his who first of you, young men, kisses his mother

phrases.latin: nēmō nostrum est īdem māne quī fuit prīdiē
phrases.english: none of us is the same in the morning as he was the day before

phrases.latin: trecentī conjūrāvimus prīncipēs juventūtis Rōmānae ut in tē hāc viā grassārēmur
phrases.english: three hundred of us, leading young men of Rome, have sworn to come at you in this way
how many of you are there?
our country is the parent of us all
